[[File:VIII The Lionsmith.png|thumb|293x293px|The Lionsmith]]
{{Quote|The Nature of the Lionsmith is to be stronger; to be seamless; to make monsters. It has been suggested that his flesh became dust in the [[Tombs of the Shadowless Kings]].}}
'''The Lionsmith''', also called '''The Golden General''', is one of the [[Hours]], associated with hour VIII, or 8:00am. His [[Aspects]] are {{Lore|Edge}}, {{Lore|Heart}}, and {{Lore|Forge}}. The Lionsmith is one of the Gods-from-Flesh, and he makes monsters such as {{Lore|Edge|Labhitic Grains|Labhites}}, {{Lore|Edge|Skaptodon Fang|Skaptodons}} and cats. According to ''[[The Tantra of Worms]]'', the Lionsmith is capable of crushing Worms, a feat that would be impossible for normal mortals.

The Lionsmith has a legendary rivalry with [[The Colonel]]. Supposedly, in the First History, the Lionsmith was a mortal from the [[Shadowless Empire]] who traveled to the kingdom of the Perseids to learn from The Colonel, swearing loyalty to him. When he returned to the Shadowless Empire, he led their armies as The Golden General until the empire was attacked by forces led by The Colonel. According to ''[[The Book of Thrones]]'', he was unwilling to take arms against The Colonel until the King of Kings of the [[Shadowless Empire]] told him "a great secret of betrayal". The secret is unknown, but [[Captain Welland]] tells it to the player when he is defeated. This led him to turn against The Colonel (perhaps at the [[wikipedia:Battle_of_Issus|Battle of Issus]], as hinted by the painting [[Masterpiece#Colonel and Lionsmith|Colonel and Lionsmith]]). When he did so, he [[Rites#Rite of the Rebel Striving|shattered his sword]], thereby enacting a potent mystery of [[The Forge of Days]] and ascending to Hour-hood. The {{Lore|Edge|Furious Sliver|fragments of this sword}} still exist.

==Notes==
*The "XIII" in the final illustration for The Lionsmith is presumed to be an error, as it would overlap with [[The Horned-Axe]]. The original concept art for The Lionsmith uses "VIII", a number which is otherwise unused. This is particularly obvious if considered in relation to the tarot, as this card very clearly relates to the Strength card in its design, which is numbered VIII.
